en.html:
Alone.
I walked the forest path.

It was hard. My body was heavy, my awareness thin, and the surroundings had somehow become terribly cold.

I suffered.
Because my life was running out.

Because I was forcing a heart that wanted to stop to keep moving. Trying to remain alive. Stop that foolish business, and surely the suffering would end at once.

But not yet. I was not permitted to die until I returned to her.

en.html:
Rousing strength I did not have, I lifted my body. Clenched my teeth and braced my one remaining arm.

Stand.
Live.

Only a little farther. Until I reached her.
Kanae Ootori.

She was an avenger. The one who would judge Kageaki Minato's crimes. The person who would give him his rightful death.

My life had to be offered to her blade. She would take it on account of the unappeased grief of someone I had killed.

She would show the anger of good against evil.

Justice existed in this world.
Evil would certainly receive its due.

I believed it.
Wanted to believe it.

So this life must end by her hand.

en.html:
I conveyed my hope.
—Judgment. Condemnation.

Whether a voice came out, I did not know. But I felt no anxiety.

She was a pure executor of vengeance. It would be all right.

I trusted her.

My understanding of Kanae Ootori's personality, which must have been complicated, was not particularly deep. There were surely many things I did not know.

Perhaps she possessed an appalling nature utterly opposed to human morality. Perhaps she was a demon with a human face and a beast's heart.

Looking back, there had certainly been glimpses to suggest it.

...But none of that had mattered.

It had not mattered, so I had paid it no attention.

en.html:
Which had been the greater fool?

He, who fought Kanae while trying to protect her?
Or Kanae, who concealed the truth, made him do so, and had him kill her?

Well.
...Much the same, perhaps.

Two hopeless fools had killed each other. And, very satisfactorily, both had died.

Surely that was all it was.

She had no fear of dying.
No complaint either.

To live was to die.
To die was to live.

The meaning was the same. Only the words differed.

Whether one regarded life as beginning at zero or moving toward zero: that was the only difference. So there was no essential difference between seeking death and seeking life.

No use clinging to a difference that amounted to wordplay. Live rightly as oneself and die rightly; that was enough.

And this end was undoubtedly the right conclusion for Kanae Ootori.
For Kageaki Minato also.

They had lived single-mindedly.
Died single-mindedly.

As Kanae Ootori.
As Kageaki Minato.

So she thought.

　そしてめでたく、どちらも死んだ。

　これはきっと、それだけのことだ。

　死にゆくことに、怖れはなかった。
　不平もなかった。

　生きるとは、死ぬということ。
　死ぬとは、生きるということ。

　意味は同じ。
　言葉が違うだけ。

　人生をゼロから発したものと見るか、ゼロへ向かう
ものと見るか、ただそれだけの違い。
　だから死を求めることと、生を求めることとの間に、
本質の差は何も無いのだ。

　そんな言葉遊び程度の違いに拘泥しても仕方ない。
　<ruby>自己<rt>おのれ</rt></ruby>として正しく生きて、正しく死ぬなら、それで
良い。

　そしてこの最期は間違いなく、大鳥香奈枝にとって
正しい帰結。
　湊斗景明の最期もそう。

　<ruby>直向<rt>ひたむき</rt></ruby>に生きた。
　直向に死んだ。

　大鳥香奈枝として。
　湊斗景明として。

　そう思う。

She spoke to him, though he would answer no more.

We were foolish.
Truly foolish.

But this was the only way we could do it, was it not?
We could not choose another road.

The two of us met, and died together—
And made this farce.

So stupid, so ridiculous, yet there is no audience.
We are alone together.
